paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's name is not a small thing. In this passage a man curses the Name, and the LORD says, "Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must surely be put to death" (Leviticus 24:16). This is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. But it shows how seriously the LORD wants His own name treated, and a baker who sees that learns to handle God's name with care.

Now look at what the LORD does next. He moves from words to lives, to injuries, to animals, and the penalty always fits what was done. "Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth" (Leviticus 24:20). Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death (Leviticus 24:21). I think the LORD is showing that a human life is worth far more than an animal's, and that the punishment is never bigger than the wrong.

And then comes the line that holds it all together: "You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God" (Leviticus 24:22). Nobody gets a softer rule and nobody gets a harder one. Same standard, because He is the LORD their God. So when you open your Bible, friend, take God's name seriously, treat every person's life as precious, and remember that the One who sets the standard is the same for everybody.
